_readme.what: Hand corrections merged over build_author_table.py's Wikidata resolution, and winning.
_readme.why: A Wiktionary attribution is not always an rdfs:label: it can name a writing duo, use a title the label spells differently, or be a bare pen name. Each entry below was checked against Wikidata by hand on 2026-09-20; the QID and death year are quoted from the item named.
_readme.joint_attributions: Where a reference names two authors, death_year is the LATER of the two deaths, because the quotation leaves copyright only when both have.
_readme.shape: Every other key is an author name exactly as it appears in a reference, mapping to { qid, label, death_year, status, note }.

Alexandre Dumas.label: Alexandre Dumas (père)
Alexandre Dumas.note: Four humans carry this label. An unqualified 'Alexandre Dumas' is conventionally père (Q38337, d. 1870); fils is Q169150 (d. 1895). Both died well before 1931, so the public-domain verdict is the same whichever the reference meant.

Comtesse de Ségur.label: comtesse de Ségur
Comtesse de Ségur.note: Wikidata spells the label with a lowercase c ('comtesse de Ségur'), so the exact-label query missed it.

Erckmann-Chatrian.label: Erckmann-Chatrian
Erckmann-Chatrian.note: A writing duo, so the item itself carries no death date. Émile Erckmann (Q3246593) died 1899, Alexandre Chatrian (Q2833544) died 1890; the later death governs.

Gustave Flaubert et Maxime Du Camp.label: Gustave Flaubert et Maxime Du Camp
Gustave Flaubert et Maxime Du Camp.note: Joint attribution: Flaubert (Q43444) died 1880, Du Camp (Q918268) died 1894; the later death governs. The qid names Du Camp, the author the year comes from.

Sidonie-Gabrielle Colette.label: Colette
Sidonie-Gabrielle Colette.note: Wikidata labels her by her pen name alone. Died 1954, so her quotations are NOT public domain under the 1931 rule.
